items.title: The State of Digital Sovereignty in Sweden
items.summary: Over the past decades, organizations have gradually lost control over the software, infrastructure, and data they depend on. Today, digital sovereignty has become a key concern for Swedish organizations facing increasing demands for compliance, data protection, and regulatory control. This session explores how we arrived here, what sovereignty means in practice, and how open technologies such as OpenStack, Ceph, Kubernetes, and open-source software can help organizations regain control of their digital future. Through practical examples, we will examine the role of data residency, access control, auditability, and modern infrastructure in building a more sovereign and resilient cloud strategy. Takeaways An understanding of the current state of digital sovereignty in Sweden and the factors driving growing interest in sovereign cloud and data control. Practical insights into how open-source technologies and open infrastructure can help organizations regain control of their data, compliance, and digital services. Key considerations for evaluating cloud strategies in relation to data residency, regulatory requirements, and long-term digital resilience.
